people.title: People
people.note: Changing a role is a governed action. It passes IAM and writes an audit record.

inUse.title: Roles in use
inUse.footer: {agents, plural, one {# agent role is} other {# agent roles are}} on the Roles tab.

people.twoFactorUnrecorded: No contract records a member's two-factor method yet, so this filter cannot narrow the list.

actions.readOnly: An owner or an admin makes these changes.
actions.denied: Changing a role and removing a member are Owner and Admin actions.

fields.name: Name
fields.mainRepoHint: owner/name on GitHub. This is where the workspace keeps .oxagen/, and it cannot change here later. The Oxagen GitHub App has to be installed on that owner and reachable from a GitHub account this organization has connected. Oxagen finds the installation from the owner.
fields.productionBranchHint: The only branch whose commits update the code graph. A re-approval on the Repositories page moves it.
fields.productionBranchCreateHint: The only branch whose commits update the code graph. If GitHub’s default changes later you are prompted; the binding never moves on its own.
fields.retentionHint: content_exact keeps prompts and tool bodies in full. digest_only lowers the replay grade. No contract records the mode per workspace yet.
fields.mainRepoFixed: Changing main is an org-owner action with approval.
fields.namespaceHint: Immutable. It is in every agent key in this workspace.
fields.namespaceCreateHint: 2 to 6 characters, immutable, and part of every agent key in the workspace. Oxagen derives it from the name when it creates the workspace, and Create a workspace takes none yet (#3933).
fields.mainRepoSelectHint: Required at creation. A workspace without a main repo cannot exist.

governance.heading: Governance mode
governance.about: Written to .oxagen/rules/governance.toml on the main repository through a Context PR. It takes effect on merge. The mode decides who merges a Context PR in this workspace.
governance.solo: solo · The author may merge their own.
governance.team: team · A code-owner review is required.
governance.regulated: regulated · A named approver from a role must approve, and the promotion ledger is hash-chained.
governance.overrideHint: Under team or regulated the change goes to a pull request for someone else to merge. You may commit it straight to the production branch instead. The skipped review is recorded against your name.

done.applied: {mode} is in force now, committed to {branch} on {repo}.
done.overridden: You committed it without the review the previous mode asked for. That is recorded as steering.governance_overridden.
done.proposed: The change to {mode} is waiting on a pull request against {branch}. It is not in force until someone merges it on GitHub.
done.reused: It updated the pull request already open on oxagen/governance.
done.refused: The name was saved. The governance mode was not changed: {reason}

governance.createHint: Set it from Edit once the workspace exists. Create a workspace takes no governance mode yet.

archiveWorkspace.title: Archive workspace
archiveWorkspace.body: Archiving freezes {name}: runs, frames, records and spend stay readable forever. Its API keys stop working while it is archived. None of them is revoked, so restoring the workspace brings them back.
archiveWorkspace.agents: {more, select, yes {At least {count} agents are} other {{count, plural, one {# agent is} other {# agents are}}}} registered here. Deregister or move them first.
archiveWorkspace.noAgents: No agents here. Archiving is an owner or admin action, recorded as a security event.
archiveWorkspace.agentsUnread: Registered agents are not readable without membership here. Archive is refused while any agent is registered.

role.title: Change role
role.note: A grant is a governed action, not a settings change. It writes an audit record. It does not widen what their agents may do: an agent’s effective permission is its own grants intersected with the operator’s.
role.label: Role

remove.title: Remove from the organization
remove.body: {name} loses <mono>{role}</mono> and every workspace grant. Their sessions end now.
remove.note: Removing is a governed action and is recorded. Oxagen revokes the command-line keys they minted, and runs stay attributed to them. Which agents act on their behalf is not recorded here yet (#3932).

failure.orgRoleRequired: Denied. An owner or an admin makes this change.
failure.noPrincipal: The request carried no signed-in user. Sign in and try again.
failure.delegationCeiling: Denied. A role cannot grant more than you hold. Drop the permissions you do not hold, or ask an owner.
failure.roleExists: That name is taken in this organization. Pick another.
failure.roleNotFound: This organization has no role by that name. Nothing was changed.
failure.roleInUse: Principals still hold this role. Reassign them, then delete it.
failure.systemRoleReadonly: Built-in roles are read-only. Duplicate this one to change its permissions.
failure.slugTaken: A workspace in this organization already has that address. Pick another name.
failure.workspaceNotFound: That workspace has left this organization. Reload the page.
failure.workspaceHasAgents: Agents are still registered in this workspace. Deregister or move them, then archive it.
failure.invalid: The request was refused as invalid. Nothing was changed.
failure.pendingApproval: The change is waiting for approval, request {accessRequestId}.
failure.unavailable: The change could not be made: {code}. Nothing was changed.
failure.refused: The change was refused: {code}. Nothing was changed.
failure.lastOwner: This is the last owner of the organization. Make someone else an owner first.
failure.targetNotMember: This person is no longer a member of this organization.
failure.roleNotGrantable: That role is not one this organization grants. Nothing was changed.
failure.insufficientRole: Your organization role does not allow this change. Nothing was changed.
failure.githubNotAuthorized: This organization has not connected GitHub, so the repository cannot be reached. Connect GitHub from a workspace’s settings, then try again.
failure.installationUnreachable: The Oxagen GitHub App is not installed on that owner, or the connected GitHub account cannot reach it. Install the App on the owner, then try again.
failure.repositoryNotInstalled: The App’s installation on that owner cannot see that repository. Grant it access on GitHub, then try again.
failure.mainRepoClaimed: Another workspace already steers by that repository. A repository is the main repository of one workspace.
failure.repositoryLinkedElsewhere: Another workspace has linked that repository, so it cannot be a main repository. A main repository holds the .oxagen/ tree, and a linked one receives another workspace’s Context PRs.
failure.repositoryUnparsable: That is not a repository name GitHub accepts. Write it as owner/name.
failure.ssoProviderNotFound: This identity provider no longer exists. Reload the page.
failure.ssoRequiresEnterprise: Single sign-on is part of the Enterprise plan. Upgrade the organization to set it up.
failure.scimTokenExists: The organization already has a SCIM token. Rotate it to get a new one.
failure.scimTokenChanged: Another change to the SCIM token finished first. Reload the page and try again.

invitations.title: Pending invitations
invitations.empty: No invitations are waiting for an answer.
invitations.resent: Invitation email sent. It expires in seven days.
invitations.deliveryFailed: The invitation now expires in seven days, but its email could not be sent. Resend to try again.
invitations.confirmBody: The link stops working the moment this is revoked, and {email} gets no notice. Nothing is created for them, so nothing is left behind.
invitations.confirmNote: Who invited them, when, and who revoked it stay in the audit record. Inviting them again issues a new link.

invite.title: Invite a person
invite.body: An invitation is the only way into the organization. It expires in seven days, and accepting it requires a verified email.
invite.denied: Inviting someone is an Owner and Admin action.

sent.title: Invitation sent
sent.body: {email} was invited as {role}. The invitation is listed under Pending invitations until they answer.

already.title: Already invited
already.body: {email} already has a pending invitation, so nothing changed. It is listed under Pending invitations, and the role it offers is the one it was sent with.

failure.emailInvalid: That is not an email address. Check the spelling and try again.
failure.roleNotInvitable: That role is not one an invitation offers. Pick Member, Admin, or Owner.

invite.bodyTwoFactor: An invitation is the only way into the organization. It expires in seven days, and accepting it requires a verified email and two-factor.

create.title: Create an API key
create.body: The key acts as you. Oxagen shows the secret once and stores only its prefix and a hash, so a lost key is rotated, never recovered.
create.name: Name

rotate.title: Rotate this key
rotate.body: This issues a replacement with the same expiry and ends this key in the same transaction. Requests presenting the old key are refused from that moment, so put the new one in place first. An expired key cannot be rotated, because the replacement would carry the expiry that ended it.

revoke.title: Revoke this key
revoke.body: Every request presenting this key is refused from this moment. The row stays in the record with the time it ended. Only a new key restores access.

secret.title: Copy the key now
secret.body: This is the only time Oxagen shows it. Close this and the secret is gone from here for good.

failure.denied: Your organization role does not allow this. Nothing was changed.
failure.keyNotFound: This key is no longer here, or it was already revoked.
failure.keyExpired: This key expired while the page was open. Rotating it would copy the expiry that ended it onto the replacement, so nothing was changed. Create a new key instead.
failure.nameRequired: Give the key a name so the roster can tell it apart.
failure.expiryNotADay: That expiry is not a date. Pick a day, or leave it empty for a key that does not expire.
failure.expiryInThePast: That day is already over. Pick a later one, or leave it empty for a key that does not expire.
failure.refused: The change was refused: {code}. Nothing was changed.
failure.invalid: The request was refused as invalid. Nothing was changed.
failure.pendingApproval: The change is waiting for approval, request {accessRequestId}.
failure.unavailable: The change could not be made: {code}. Nothing was changed.
failure.workspaceArchived: That workspace was archived while this page was open. Its keys are listed so they can be revoked; no new key is issued into it.

workspace.label: Workspace
workspace.archivedNote: This workspace is archived. Its keys stop working while it is archived and are listed so they can be revoked. No new key is issued into it.

noWorkspace.title: A key needs a workspace
noWorkspace.body: A key is issued into one workspace and acts only there. This organization has no workspace you are a member of, so there is nowhere to issue one yet.

apiKeys.empty: This workspace has no API keys.

denied.title: You cannot see this organization’s API keys
denied.body: Signed in as {role}. Needed: {permission}. An owner can grant it, and the grant is recorded in the audit record.

pending.title: Waiting for approval
pending.body: Access request {id} is waiting for an owner’s decision.

error.title: API keys could not be loaded
error.body: {status} {code}. Nothing was changed. Reload the page to try again.

apiKeys.emptyFiltered: Every key in this workspace has been revoked or has expired. Choose All to see {ended, plural, one {it} other {them}}.
apiKeys.title: API keys
apiKeys.caption: each key acts as the person who created it
apiKeys.note: A key is shown once, at creation, and never again. Until keys carry grants of their own, a key acts as the person who created it, in its workspace. Revoking a key ends its access at the next call.

state.expiring: {days, plural, one {expires in # day} other {expires in # days}}

surfaces.title: Surfaces this reaches
surfaces.body: One agent tool contract drives the API, MCP, the CLI and these screens, so a key that can do something here can do exactly that much everywhere else. Parity is checked by the manifest gate.

roleCatalog.title: Roles

enforcement.enforced: Oxagen checks these grants on governed calls.
enforcement.recorded: recorded for people, enforced for agents. On the {tier} tier Oxagen allows a person every governed action whatever a role says. An agent is checked on every tier: its own grants and the grants of the person it acts for both bound what it may do.

roleCatalog.deleteHeld: {count, plural, one {Reassign the # holder first} other {Reassign the # holders first}}
roleCatalog.note: A role is a permission set, nothing more. An agent’s effective permission is its roles ∩ its operator’s grants ∩ the policy bundle ∩ the kill switches. A role can widen what an agent may ask for, never what its operator may.

editor.name: Role name
editor.nameNewHint: Immutable once created. Use the kind as the prefix: agent., org., workspace., svc.
editor.nameHint: Names are immutable. Duplicate the role to rename it.
editor.descriptionFixed: The description is set when the role is created. No capability changes it yet (#4038).
editor.kindHint: Who can hold it. A custom role is held by agents, which assign_agent_role binds. Human roles wait on #4038, and service roles on #3937.
editor.scopeHint: An organization role applies everywhere. A workspace role is assigned in one workspace at a time.
editor.holders: {count, plural, one {Held by # principal} other {Held by # principals}}. Saving changes their effective permission at the next call, and nothing in flight is cut.
editor.governed: Saving is a governed action. It passes IAM and writes an audit record. org.* is the only wildcard and only org.owner carries it.

del.title: Delete role
del.body: This removes {name} from IAM. Its definition and every grant it carried stay in the audit record.
del.held: {count, plural, one {Held by # principal} other {Held by # principals}}. Reassign them first, because a role cannot be deleted out from under a holder.
del.free: Nobody holds it. Deleting is a governed action and is recorded.

workspaces.title: Workspaces
workspaces.note: Changing which repository is main is an org-owner action with approval, recorded as a security event. A repository may be linked to more than one workspace; it is main for at most one.

openrouter.name: OpenRouter
openrouter.hint: One key reaches every model. Embeddings stay on Oxagen's key and are billed.

gateway.name: Vercel AI Gateway
gateway.hint: One key reaches every model, embeddings included.

openai.name: OpenAI
openai.hint: Your OpenAI key. Name the model the assistant should use.

anthropic.name: Anthropic
anthropic.hint: Your Anthropic key. Name the model the assistant should use.
anthropic.caching: Oxagen reaches Anthropic through its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, which has no prompt caching. An OpenRouter or Vercel AI Gateway key keeps caching on Claude models.

openai_compatible.name: Other OpenAI-compatible server
openai_compatible.hint: Together, Fireworks, Groq, Azure, or your own server. Give its URL and model.

form.keyHint: Oxagen calls the model with it once to check it works, then stores it encrypted. It is never returned to a screen and never read from the environment.
form.baseUrlHint: Must start with https and be reachable on the public internet.
form.balancedHint: Required. The assistant runs on this model.
form.unmappedNote: Any model you leave blank uses the balanced model.
form.saved: Key saved. The next assistant turn uses it.

verdict.ok: The vendor accepted the key ({ms} ms).
verdict.okWithTools: The vendor accepted the key and the model can use tools ({ms} ms).
verdict.noTools: The key works, but this model cannot use tools, so the assistant cannot answer questions about your workspace with it. Choose a model that supports tool calls. The vendor said: {reason}

remove.label: Remove the key
remove.confirm: Remove the key? Your organization's next turn runs on Oxagen's key and is billed.

failure.denied: Only an organization owner or admin can change this.
failure.keyRequired: Paste a key of at least 8 characters.
failure.balancedRequired: Enter the model the assistant should use.
failure.invalid: Oxagen refused these settings. Check that the URL starts with https and is not a private address.
failure.pendingApproval: This change is waiting for approval.
failure.unavailable: Oxagen could not reach the key service ({code}). Try again.

funding.title: Funding source
funding.unknown: Oxagen pays for this organization’s model calls, on its minted key or on the shared key. No capability reads which one yet (#4005), so no source is chosen here.
funding.preview: Preview of {source}. The recorded source is {current}, and this page cannot switch it yet (#4005).
funding.note: No call reads the environment. Keys and routes come from the model layer’s resolver, and a path that bypasses it is a defect.

platform_minted.option: platform_minted — one key minted for this organization on Oxagen’s OpenRouter account
platform_minted.summary: One key minted for this organization on Oxagen’s OpenRouter account.
platform_minted.about: Oxagen owns, pays, rotates and revokes it. Its tokens are billed. The provider reports it on its own line, so the bill and the ledger can be compared.

platform.about: One key for every customer. Its tokens are billed. The provider returns one total for every customer, so Oxagen’s meter is the only record of this organization’s share.

customer_key.option: customer_key — your own OpenRouter or vendor key
customer_key.summary: Your own OpenRouter or vendor key.
customer_key.about: You own and pay for it. Oxagen stores it encrypted and never returns it. Your vendor bills these tokens and Oxagen charges nothing for them.

customer.billing: your vendor bills these tokens and Oxagen charges nothing for them
customer.storage: encrypted under the organization’s key and never returned to a screen

shared.billing: Oxagen pays the provider and bills the tokens as assistant usage

minted.unrecorded: No capability returns this organization’s minted key yet, so its facts are not recorded here (#4005).

mint.title: Mint a model key for {org}
mint.body: Oxagen would call OpenRouter’s provisioning API, mint a key named for this organization with a spend cap set at the provider, and store it encrypted. Minting would be a governed action with your name on it. No capability mints a key from this page yet, so nothing is sent (#4005).

rotate.title: Rotate this key
rotate.body: Rotation would provision a new key at the provider, then revoke the old one once the engine has picked the new one up. Turns in flight would finish on the key they started with. No capability rotates the minted key yet, so nothing is sent (#4005).

revoke.title: Revoke this key
revoke.body: Revoking would end the key at the provider at the next call, and the in-app agent would stop for everyone in {org}. No capability revokes the minted key yet, so nothing is sent (#4005).

minted.noKey: No capability reads whether a key is held for {org} yet (#4005). With no key the in-app agent cannot run, and nothing has been charged. Minting one is a governed action and puts your name on it.

change.title: Change funding source
change.note: Pick a source on the panel behind this dialog. It carries the key field and the lifecycle. On a customer key your vendor bills the tokens and Oxagen charges nothing for them. On the other two they are billed to this organization.

reconciliation.title: Reconciliation
reconciliation.note: Two independent numbers: the first is read off the provider’s usage report for this key, the second is summed from Oxagen’s own ledger. No capability reads either for this organization yet (#4005).

funding.unknownPreview: Preview of {source}. No capability reads which source pays for this organization yet (#4005).

routes.title: Model routes
routes.caption: customer agents call their providers with their own keys
routes.harnesses: These routes carry Oxagen’s own work. Oxagen records what each harness reports.

tiers.complex: reflection, promotion rationale, Context PR bodies, run names and summaries
tiers.light: classification, labeling, entity and property naming, redaction hints, approval summaries, reranking
tiers.embed: embeddings for entities, records, documents, issues, code

routes.unrecorded: Oxagen’s own model routes are not stored per organization yet, and no read returns a tier’s use or cost this month (#4006).

edit.title: Edit the {tier} route
edit.body: Saving would set this tier’s provider, route and fallback for the organization, recorded as a control-plane event and applied at the next model call. No capability stores a route yet, so nothing is sent (#4006).

sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.intro: Let members sign in with your company identity provider. Add an OIDC or SAML provider for your email domain, publish one DNS record to prove you own the domain, then map the provider's groups to roles on the Roles tab.
sso.readOnly: Only an Owner or an Admin can change single sign-on.

denied.title: Owners and Admins only
denied.body: Single sign-on settings are visible to Owners and Admins. Ask one of them for access.

plan.notice: Single sign-on is part of the Enterprise plan.
plan.lapsed: Your providers no longer sign anyone in. You can still delete them.

providers.title: Identity providers
providers.empty: No identity provider yet. A provider lets members sign in with your company identity provider instead of a password.

setup.title: Setup for {name}
setup.dnsLead: Publish this TXT record at your DNS host, then verify the domain. The provider signs nobody in until the domain is verified.
setup.dnsVerified: Domain verified. Members with a {domain} address can sign in through this provider.
setup.idpLead: Paste these into your identity provider's application settings.
setup.copyFailed: Copy failed. Select the text instead.

policy.title: Sign-in policy
policy.label: Require SSO for members
policy.on: Members other than Owners must sign in through one of your providers.
policy.off: Members can sign in with a password or through a provider.
policy.owners: Owners can always sign in with a password, so an identity provider outage cannot lock your organization out.
policy.needsVerified: Verify a provider's domain before you require SSO.
policy.lapsed: Require SSO does not apply on your current plan. Turn it off to clear it.

form.providerIdHint: Lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens. It appears in the callback URL and cannot change.
form.domainHint: People with an address at this domain sign in through this provider. It cannot change after you add the provider.
form.groupsClaimHint: The claim or attribute that carries the person's groups.
form.issuerHint: Oxagen reads the issuer's discovery document when you save.
form.certHint: The identity provider's X.509 certificate, in PEM format.
form.certEditHint: Paste the certificate again to change the entity ID, the SSO URL, or the private key.
form.spPrivateKeyHint: Optional. PEM. Oxagen signs its sign-in requests with this key.
form.stored: Stored. Leave blank to keep it.

delete.title: Delete {name}
delete.body: Members stop signing in through this provider, and its group mappings are removed. If it is your last verified provider, SSO stops being required.

failure.denied: Only an Owner or an Admin can change single sign-on.
failure.invalid: Check this value and try again.
failure.invalidSettings: Oxagen could not use these settings. For OIDC, check that the issuer URL serves a discovery document. For SAML, check the SSO URL and the certificate.
failure.certRequiredForChange: Paste the signing certificate to save a change to the SAML settings.
failure.dnsRecordNotFound: The TXT record was not found. DNS changes can take a few minutes to reach Oxagen. Check the name and value, then try again.
failure.noVerifiedProvider: Verify a provider's domain before you require SSO.
failure.providerIdTaken: A provider with this ID already exists. Choose another ID.
failure.providerIdReserved: This ID belongs to another sign-in method. Choose another ID.
failure.domainTaken: Another provider already uses this email domain.
failure.notFound: This provider no longer exists. Reload the page.
failure.pendingApproval: The change is waiting for approval.
failure.unavailable: The change could not be saved ({code}). Try again.
failure.requiresEnterprise: Single sign-on is part of the Enterprise plan. Upgrade the organization to set it up.
failure.scimTokenExists: The organization already has a SCIM token. Rotate it to get a new one.

scim.title: SCIM provisioning
scim.lead: Your identity provider can create people in Oxagen before they sign in, and remove them when they leave. Removing someone ends their sessions, revokes their API keys and machine keys, and removes their roles and membership. Groups decide roles through the IdP group mappings on the Roles tab.
scim.none: No SCIM token. Generate one, then enter it with the base URL in your identity provider.
scim.once: Copy this token now. Oxagen stores only its hash and cannot show it again.
scim.rotateBody: The current token stops working at once. Enter the new token in your identity provider before its next push.
scim.revokeBody: Your identity provider can no longer create or remove people. People it already created keep their access.
scim.readOnly: Only an Owner or an Admin can manage the SCIM token.

ssoGroups.title: IdP group mappings
ssoGroups.lead: Map each identity provider group to an organization role.
ssoGroups.rules: A group with no row grants nothing. A person whose groups match no row loses their organization role at their next SSO sign-in. When a person's groups match more than one row, the highest role wins.
ssoGroups.openSso: Add one on the Single sign-on page.
ssoGroups.empty: No mappings. Nobody gets a role through this provider.
ssoGroups.saved: Mappings saved. They apply at each person's next SSO sign-in.

failure.groupDuplicate: This group already has a row. Give each group one role.

costCenters.title: Cost centers
costCenters.lead: Spend is charged to the agent's cost center, or to its workspace's when the agent names none. Spend with neither is shown on Spend as its own row.
costCenters.empty: This organization has no cost centers.

add.title: Add a cost center
add.label: Label
add.labelHint: Up to 64 letters, digits, dots, underscores or hyphens, such as ENG-1001.

delete.title: Delete {label}
delete.body: Runs already rolled up keep this label. New runs from an agent or workspace that names it fall back to the workspace's cost center, or to none.

charge.title: Cost center for {name}
charge.label: Cost center
charge.hint: Runs rolled up after this change are charged to the new label.

page.description: People, roles, workspaces, model routes, the data plane, and API keys.

empty.title: This organization has no workspaces
empty.body: A workspace owns one main repo, one steering set, a set of agents, tool grants, and budgets. A workspace without a main repo cannot exist.

error.title: Organization could not be loaded
error.body: Nothing was changed. Runs kept recording while this page was down. Frames are written by the collector on each host, not by Oxagen.

denied.title: You cannot see this organization’s settings
denied.needed: org.admin (members, funding, and the data plane are owner-only)
denied.grant: An organization owner can grant it; the grant is a governed action and lands in the audit record with your name on it.
denied.decider: the organization role check on the server · deny wins over every allow

requestAccess.title: Request access
requestAccess.body: Request access would ask an owner of {org} to grant you org.admin, and the grant would land in the audit record. No capability records that request yet, so nothing is sent from here. Ask an owner to change your role on the People tab.

incident.title: Open an incident
incident.body: Open an incident would file one carrying the code and the instant below. No capability files incidents yet, so nothing is sent from here. Report it by hand with this line: {line}

dataPlane.title: Data plane
dataPlane.preview: Preview. This organization is on {mode}, so these facts describe what {other} would be.

about.shared: Tenant data on Oxagen’s shared plane, isolated by row-level security with no bypass setting.
about.dedicated: Tenant data on a Postgres the organization controls, bound per organization and resolved at every call.
about.firewall: The whole data plane inside the customer’s network, delivered as a signed bundle.

retention.title: Retention
retention.note: Replay without bodies is a timeline, not a replay. The explanation promise depends on bodies, so keeping them is the default.

isolation.title: Tenant isolation
isolation.rowsValue: every tenant table carries org_id and row-level security is on with no bypass. The tenant boundary is the policy, and the policy is tested.
isolation.workspaceScopingValue: every run, frame and record carries its workspace, set by the kernel, the only writer
isolation.crossTenantValue: refused by the database itself, not by application code
isolation.platformCatalogsValue: price books, tool schemas and connector definitions are platform tables, never tenant rows
isolation.startupGuardValue: the app role may not be a superuser, may not hold BYPASSRLS, and row-level security may not be off, or the plane refuses to boot

plane.title: Request a change of data plane
plane.body: A change of plane would be requested here and decided by Oxagen, then applied with set_data_plane. No capability records the request yet, so nothing is sent. The binding is set today through set_data_plane on the API, MCP or the CLI by an owner or an admin.

rotate.title: Rotate keys
rotate.body: Rotate keys would rotate this organization’s key-encryption key and land on Audit under Keys. No capability rotates it yet, so nothing is sent from here.

dataPlane.identityShared: stay on the shared plane by design

receipts.saved: Saved. Recorded in the audit record.
receipts.roleChanged: {name} now holds {role}. Recorded in the audit record.
receipts.memberRemoved: {name} was removed from the organization. Recorded in the audit record.
receipts.invited: Invitation sent to {email}. Recorded in the audit record.
receipts.invitationResent: Invitation sent again. Recorded in the audit record.
receipts.invitationRevoked: Invitation revoked. Recorded in the audit record.
receipts.roleCreated: {name} was created. Recorded in the audit record.
receipts.roleSaved: {name} was saved. Each holder's permission changes at their next call. Recorded in the audit record.
receipts.roleDeleted: {name} was deleted. Its definition and grants stay in the audit record.
receipts.keyCreated: {name} was created. Recorded in the audit record.
receipts.keyRotated: {name} was rotated. Recorded in the audit record.
receipts.keyRevoked: {name} was revoked. Its access ends at the next call. Recorded in the audit record.
receipts.workspaceCreated: The workspace was created. Recorded in the audit record.
receipts.workspaceSaved: {name} was saved. Recorded in the audit record.
receipts.workspaceArchived: {name} was archived. Recorded in the audit record.
receipts.modelKeySaved: Your key was saved. The next assistant turn uses it. Recorded in the audit record.
receipts.modelKeyRemoved: Your key was removed. Turns run on Oxagen's key from the next call. Recorded in the audit record.
